page.h1: HTS Chapter 30: Pharmaceutical Products — Export Markets & Foreign Tariff Rates

seo.title: Where U.S. Medicines Are Sold & the Tariff Each Country Charges (HTS Ch. 30) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The 12 largest buyers of U.S. pharmaceuticals, what each buys (vaccines, antibodies, packaged medicines), the tariff it charges by product group and the approval needed to sell there.
keywords: tariff on US medicines by country
export medicines to EU from US

intro: Who buys U.S. pharmaceuticals, **what** they buy and **what they charge** on it. The matrix shows each destination's tariff on U.S.-origin goods for the six Chapter 30 product groups, next to the value the U.S. shipped there in 2025. Below it, a short profile of each market names the regulator whose approval decides whether the product can be sold at all — for medicines that, not the tariff, is usually the real gate.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

countries.rule: EU common external tariff (WTO pharmaceutical zero-for-zero)

profile.headline: U.S. medicines enter Germany duty-free, as everywhere in the EU, and no EU measure since 2025 has changed that. The 33% jump in 2025 sales is supply-chain driven, not tariff driven.
profile.mainProducts: Vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · packaged medicines (3004)

regulator.name: European Medicines Agency (EMA) or the national agency
regulator.requirement: An EU marketing authorisation (centralised via EMA for biologics), an EU-based authorisation holder and an EU importer with a manufacturing/import authorisation; a Qualified Person certifies each batch.

countries.rule: EU common external tariff (WTO pharmaceutical zero-for-zero)

profile.headline: Duty-free. Much of what lands in the Netherlands is cleared there and then distributed across the EU, so this figure partly stands in for other EU buyers.
profile.mainProducts: Vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · packaged medicines (3004)

regulator.name: European Medicines Agency (EMA) or the national agency
regulator.requirement: An EU marketing authorisation (centralised via EMA for biologics), an EU-based authorisation holder and an EU importer with a manufacturing/import authorisation; a Qualified Person certifies each batch.

countries.rule: MFN rate plus China's extra 10% on all U.S. goods

profile.headline: China is the only big buyer charging U.S. medicines more than in January 2025: an extra 10% on top of its 0–3% normal rate. It peaked at 125% in April 2025, when some U.S. drugs reportedly got quiet exemptions; sales dipped only 4%.
profile.mainProducts: Vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · packaged medicines (3004)
profile.tariffNow: Same + 10% extra on all U.S. goods

regulator.name: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA)
regulator.requirement: An imported-drug registration with NMPA and port inspection on arrival.

profile.headline: Japan charges nothing on U.S. medicines and did not retaliate. Only a few minor 3006 lines (e.g. lubricating gels, ostomy appliances) carry 2–4%. The 15% drop in 2025 sales is not tariff driven.
profile.mainProducts: Vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · packaged medicines (3004)

regulator.name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare / PMDA
regulator.requirement: A Japanese marketing approval held by a Japan-based marketing authorisation holder.

profile.headline: U.S. medicines enter Canada duty-free, and neither the 2025 nor the 2026 Canadian counter-tariff list included a single Chapter 30 line.
profile.mainProducts: Packaged medicines (3004) · vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002)

regulator.name: Health Canada
regulator.requirement: A Drug Identification Number (DIN) and an importer holding a Drug Establishment Licence.

countries.rule: EU common external tariff (WTO pharmaceutical zero-for-zero)

profile.headline: Duty-free. Belgium is a European vaccine and biologics hub, and U.S. sales there rose 45% in 2025 with no tariff change.
profile.mainProducts: Vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · packaged medicines (3004)

regulator.name: European Medicines Agency (EMA) or the national agency
regulator.requirement: An EU marketing authorisation (centralised via EMA for biologics), an EU-based authorisation holder and an EU importer with a manufacturing/import authorisation; a Qualified Person certifies each batch.

profile.headline: Duty-free. Unlike most EU buyers, Spain mainly takes finished packaged medicines from the U.S.
profile.mainProducts: Packaged medicines (3004) · vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002)

regulator.name: European Medicines Agency (EMA) or the national agency
regulator.requirement: An EU marketing authorisation (centralised via EMA for biologics), an EU-based authorisation holder and an EU importer with a manufacturing/import authorisation; a Qualified Person certifies each batch.

countries.rule: EU common external tariff (WTO pharmaceutical zero-for-zero)

profile.headline: Duty-free. Ireland is also the largest supplier of U.S. pharmaceutical imports ($42.6B), so much of this trade is drug substance and biologics moving between plants of the same companies.
profile.mainProducts: Vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · packaged medicines (3004)

regulator.name: European Medicines Agency (EMA) or the national agency
regulator.requirement: An EU marketing authorisation (centralised via EMA for biologics), an EU-based authorisation holder and an EU importer with a manufacturing/import authorisation; a Qualified Person certifies each batch.

profile.headline: The UK charges nothing on U.S. medicines. The December 2025 pharma deal changed what the NHS pays for new medicines, not UK tariffs; the 36% drop in 2025 sales came before it.
profile.mainProducts: Packaged medicines (3004) · vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002)

regulator.name: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
regulator.requirement: A UK marketing authorisation and a UK importer licence.

countries.rule: Mercosur common external tariff (MFN); no U.S. preference

profile.headline: U.S. medicines pay Brazil’s normal Mercosur rates — near zero for most biologics, around 10% on many packaged drugs. Brazil has not retaliated, but its August 2026 reciprocity case could; suspending drug patents is one listed option.
profile.mainProducts: Packaged medicines (3004) · vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002)

regulator.name: ANVISA
regulator.requirement: Product registration with ANVISA, held by a Brazilian company.

countries.rule: MFN (zero on all industrial goods since 2024)

profile.headline: Duty-free. Switzerland abolished tariffs on all industrial goods in January 2024, and the November 2025 framework only locked that in for U.S. goods.
profile.mainProducts: Vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · packaged medicines (3004)

regulator.name: Swissmedic
regulator.requirement: A Swissmedic marketing authorisation held by a Swiss company.

profile.headline: No Mexican tariff change has touched U.S. medicines; they still enter free under USMCA. Without USMCA they would face Mexico’s MFN rates (about 5% on many biologics).
profile.mainProducts: Packaged medicines (3004) · vaccines, antibodies & blood products (3002) · bandages & dressings (3005)

regulator.name: COFEPRIS
regulator.requirement: A COFEPRIS sanitary registration and import permit.

why:
The U.S. imported $213.8B of pharmaceuticals in 2025 and exported $97.8B. Both numbers are large because the same multinational drugmakers sit on both sides of the trade, moving product between their own plants:

- **Biologics go both ways.** Vaccines, antibodies and blood products (heading 3002) were 58.6% of U.S. exports ($57.3B) and about half of imports ($109.6B). A company may make an antibody in Ireland or Germany for the U.S. market while shipping a different vaccine or plasma product from U.S. plants to Europe and Asia.
- **Drug substance and finished packs cross separately.** Bulk drug substance is often made in one country and filled, finished or packaged in another, sometimes by a contract manufacturer — so the same product can be counted as an export and later as an import.
- **Distribution hubs inflate some buyers.** The Netherlands and Belgium clear goods for the whole EU, and Ireland, Switzerland and Germany are big suppliers *and* big buyers, reflecting where companies have put plants and intellectual property.

Tariffs barely touch this trade. Under the WTO zero-for-zero pharmaceutical agreement, the EU, Japan, Canada, Switzerland and the UK charge nothing on most medicines. The exposure sits with buyers outside it: China (now an extra 10% on top of 0–3%), Brazil (up to 14%) and Mexico, where U.S. drugs are free only while USMCA lasts.
assumptions: Rates are each destination's MFN applied rate on one representative HS subheading per group (shown under each cell), from the WITS/TRAINS 2023 schedules — the latest year available for all of them. National 8–10-digit lines can differ.
EU members share one tariff, so Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain and Ireland show the same rates.
Canada and Mexico apply USMCA rates (Free) to qualifying U.S. goods; the MFN rate they would charge otherwise is noted under the cell.
China's extra 10% applies to all U.S.-origin goods on top of its MFN rate. A further 24 points are suspended until Jan 10, 2027.
Regulatory requirements are summarised for orientation only; check the regulator's current rules for the specific product.
